newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close up on technical bounce, cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close up on technical bounce, cash.

text.p: A technical bounce plus slow farmer selling and mostly firm cash basis markets boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"Some thought the market was overextended late last week and this is probably just a little recovery," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Soybeans fell last week amid fund long liquidation and forecasts for active soybean harvesting in the U.S. Midwest.
Indications the November was oversold stemmed in part from the nine day relative strength index for that month which Friday dropped below 20 points, one barometer of an oversold market.
The November RSI Monday closed at 25.146 points.
Soybeans also found support from talk that soybean yields may not be as bountiful as earlier expected.
"We're also starting to hear talk bean yields in Iowa are a little lower than expected," said O'Connor's Ron Kucha.
Soybeans closed 2-1/2 to seven cents per bushel higher, with November up seven at $7.34-1/4. January was up 6-1/2 at $7.42-1/4.
Traders said the Leslie-ADM Elevator survey results released Monday gave the soybean market little direction.
"Leslie was about as expected on beans and a little low on corn," a trader said.
The Leslie report estimated 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.302 billion bushels, about in line with other private outlooks but above USDA's September forecast for 2.270 billion bushels.
Key players Monday included Merrill Lynch Futures sale of six million November while Continental Grain and Produce Grain each sold two million bushels, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 50,000, down from 100,268 Friday.

In soybean options, Continental Grain sold 600 November $7.25 calls at 14 to 15-1/2 cents and Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp sold 400 November $7.25 puts at seven cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 26,000, down from 42,699 Friday.
